quests.instruction: A real stop sign has 8 sides. Which shape matches it exactly?
quests.hint: Count up from a hexagon's 6 sides by 2 more.
quests.explanation: A stop sign's 8 sides match an octagon exactly.
quests.funFact: Stop signs have used this same 8-sided shape in the United States for over a century.

quests.instruction: Which shape, out of Hexagon, Pentagon, and Circle, is the only one with no straight sides at all?
quests.hint: Two of these three shapes are polygons made of straight lines.
quests.explanation: A circle has no straight sides, unlike a hexagon or pentagon, which are both built from straight lines.
quests.funFact: Any shape made entirely of straight-line sides is called a polygon — and a circle is not one.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape casts a perfectly round shadow no matter which direction the light shines from?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that looks the same outline from every single angle.
quests.explanation: A sphere always casts a round shadow because it looks the same from every angle.
quests.funFact: A cube or cylinder can cast different-shaped shadows depending on the angle, but a sphere never changes.

quests.instruction: A shape has 4 equal sides and 4 lines of symmetry, and it is sitting flat on one whole side, not balanced on a corner. What shape is it?
quests.hint: Remember, a diamond and a square share the same symmetry count — but only one of them sits flat on an edge.
quests.explanation: This shape sits flat on an edge, so even with the same symmetry as a diamond, it must be a square.
quests.funFact: A square and a diamond are really the same shape, just resting differently.

quests.instruction: Out of a Triangle (3 sides), a Hexagon (6 sides), and a Pentagon (5 sides), which one has the most sides?
quests.hint: Compare the three side counts given in the question and pick the largest.
quests.explanation: With 6 sides, the hexagon has more sides than the triangle's 3 or the pentagon's 5.
quests.funFact: Comparing side counts is a handy trick for ranking shapes by complexity.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has a circle base but, unlike a cylinder, narrows smoothly all the way up to a single point?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that shares a circle base with a cylinder, but doesn't keep the same width going up.
quests.explanation: Unlike a cylinder, which keeps the same width, a cone narrows from its circle base up to one point.
quests.funFact: Both a cone and a cylinder start with a circle base, but only one of them comes to a point.

quests.instruction: Home plate on a baseball field and the outline of a simple house drawing both share which 5-sided shape?
quests.hint: Think back to the 5-sided shape that both of these real objects share.
quests.explanation: Both home plate and a simple house outline are shaped like a pentagon, with 5 sides.
quests.funFact: Spotting the same shape in very different places is a great way to remember it for good.

quests.instruction: A regular hexagon can be divided into 6 equal wedges from its center. What shape is each individual wedge?
quests.hint: Think about the small pointed piece you get from two straight center-to-corner cuts.
quests.explanation: Dividing a hexagon into 6 equal wedges from the center always creates 6 small triangles.
quests.funFact: This is exactly why bees build honeycomb the way they do — a hexagon splits neatly into triangles.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has 6 flat faces that come in 3 matching pairs, but is not required to have all 6 faces equal like a cube?
quests.hint: Think of the box-shaped solid that is a cube's more general, stretched-out cousin.
quests.explanation: A rectangular prism has 3 pairs of matching faces, without requiring every face to be an equal square like a cube.
quests.funFact: Every cube fits the definition of a rectangular prism, but not every rectangular prism is a cube.

quests.instruction: Which shape, out of Hexagon, Octagon, and Pentagon, has the most lines of symmetry?
quests.hint: For these regular shapes, more sides always means more lines of symmetry.
quests.explanation: With 8 sides and 8 lines of symmetry, the octagon beats the hexagon's 6 and the pentagon's 5.
quests.funFact: For a regular polygon, the number of sides and the number of symmetry lines are always the same.

quests.instruction: A square is rotated 45 degrees so it balances on one corner. Which shape name do people usually use for it now?
quests.hint: Think of the shape name people use once a square is tipped onto its point.
quests.explanation: Once a square is tipped to balance on one point, people usually call it a diamond instead.
quests.funFact: The shape itself hasn't changed at all — only its position has.

quests.instruction: If you slice straight through the exact middle of a sphere, no matter which direction you cut, what flat shape do you always reveal?
quests.hint: Think about the one 2D shape that always appears no matter how you slice a perfectly round solid.
quests.explanation: Slicing straight through a sphere, in any direction, always reveals a circle.
quests.funFact: This works no matter which way you turn the sphere before slicing, since every angle looks the same.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape do the ancient Egyptian monuments and some modern glass museum entrances have in common?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape with a flat base and triangle sides meeting at a single peak.
quests.explanation: Both the ancient monuments and the glass entrance share the pyramid shape, with triangle sides meeting at a peak.
quests.funFact: A famous glass pyramid entrance was built centuries after the first stone pyramids, using the very same shape.

quests.instruction: Bees build honeycomb with 6-sided cells, and some soccer ball patches also have 6 sides. What shape do they share?
quests.hint: Think of the shape that tiles perfectly with no gaps, used by both bees and ball makers.
quests.explanation: Both honeycomb cells and many soccer ball patches use the hexagon, a shape that tiles with no gaps.
quests.funFact: Nature and human design both landed on the same efficient 6-sided shape.

quests.instruction: Which shape is the only one where cutting along BOTH diagonals always creates 4 identical right-triangle pieces?
quests.hint: Think of the shape whose 4 equal sides make every diagonal cut perfectly even.
quests.explanation: A square's 4 equal sides mean both diagonal cuts always create 4 identical right-triangle pieces.
quests.funFact: A rectangle's diagonals also cross in the middle, but the 4 pieces aren't always identical unless it's a square.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape keeps the exact same circle width from its bottom all the way to its top, unlike a cone?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that never narrows, unlike its pointy cousin.
quests.explanation: Unlike a cone, which narrows to a point, a cylinder keeps the exact same circle width all the way up.
quests.funFact: This even width is exactly why cylinder-shaped cans stack so neatly.

quests.instruction: Connecting the 5 outer points of a classic star with straight lines traces out which shape around its outside?
quests.hint: Think back to the 5-sided shape that hides just outside every star's points.
quests.explanation: Connecting a star's 5 outer points with straight lines always traces a pentagon around its outside.
quests.funFact: This is the reverse of the trick you learned earlier — connecting a star's inner points also hides a smaller pentagon.

quests.instruction: A slice of pie, a mountain peak, and a folded napkin corner all share which shape?
quests.hint: Think of the shape with the fewest possible sides, appearing in all three of these real objects.
quests.explanation: A pie slice, a mountain peak, and a folded napkin corner all narrow to a single point with 3 sides, just like a triangle.
quests.funFact: The same simple shape can hide in foods, landscapes, and folded fabric alike.

quests.instruction: A shipping container, a shoebox, and a brick are all real-world examples of which solid shape?
quests.hint: Think of the box-shaped solid with 6 flat rectangle faces, in many different sizes.
quests.explanation: Shipping containers, shoeboxes, and bricks are all shaped like rectangular prisms, just in very different sizes.
quests.funFact: This shape shows up at every size, from a tiny brick to a massive shipping container.

quests.instruction: If a hexagon loses exactly one side and one corner, what shape does it become?
quests.hint: A hexagon has 6 sides — losing just one brings it down to a familiar 5-sided shape.
quests.explanation: Removing one side and one corner from a hexagon's 6 leaves 5, turning it into a pentagon.
quests.funFact: Counting sides up or down by one is a reliable way to move between neighboring polygons.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape has the special property that every single point on its surface is exactly the same distance from the center?
quests.hint: Think of the solid version of a circle, but round in three dimensions instead of just two.
quests.explanation: A sphere's entire surface sits exactly the same distance from its center, in every direction.
quests.funFact: This equal-distance rule is the mathematical definition of a sphere.

quests.instruction: Which shape, out of Square, Hexagon, and Octagon, would look the roundest if it had many more sides added to it?
quests.hint: The shape closest to looking like a circle already has the most sides of the three.
quests.explanation: With the most sides of the three, an octagon already looks the closest to round, and would look even more circular with more sides.
quests.funFact: As a regular polygon gains more and more sides, it eventually starts to look just like a circle.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape, if you shrank a rectangular prism until all its sides matched exactly, would you end up with?
quests.hint: Think of the special rectangular prism where every single side has become equal.
quests.explanation: Shrinking a rectangular prism until every side matches exactly turns it into a cube.
quests.funFact: A cube is really just a perfectly balanced, special case of a rectangular prism.

quests.instruction: Two overlapping triangles, one flipped upside down, form a 6-pointed star. What shape is each of the two overlapping pieces alone?
quests.hint: Think of the shape used twice, once right-side up and once upside down.
quests.explanation: Each of the two overlapping pieces that form a 6-pointed star is, on its own, simply a triangle.
quests.funFact: Overlapping two simple triangles is all it takes to create a striking 6-pointed star pattern.

quests.instruction: A rectangle that is exactly twice as long as it is wide can always be split into two of which shape?
quests.hint: Think back to the special rectangle that splits perfectly in half.
quests.explanation: Cutting this special rectangle exactly in half, the short way, always produces two identical squares.
quests.funFact: This trick only works when a rectangle's long side is exactly double its short side.

quests.instruction: A regular pentagon, unlike a square or rectangle, cannot tile a floor without leaving gaps. What shape is being described here?
quests.hint: Think of the 5-sided shape that, despite being neat and regular, doesn't fit together with copies of itself.
quests.explanation: A regular pentagon is the shape described — its 5 sides don't fit together with copies of itself without leaving gaps.
quests.funFact: This is a surprising fact, since squares, triangles, and hexagons all tile perfectly, but regular pentagons do not.

quests.instruction: Which solid shape can you make by stacking many identical circles directly on top of each other, all the way up?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape built from a tall tower of equal-sized circles.
quests.explanation: Stacking many identical circles straight up builds a cylinder.
quests.funFact: If the circles shrank a little with each layer instead of staying equal, you'd build a cone instead.

quests.instruction: Which shape can be built from exactly 6 equilateral triangles, all meeting at one shared center point?
quests.hint: Think of the honeycomb-style shape made from six matching triangle wedges.
quests.explanation: Arranging exactly 6 equilateral triangles with their points meeting at the center builds a hexagon.
quests.funFact: This is the reverse of slicing a hexagon into triangle wedges from its center.

quests.instruction: Which shape has both 4 equal sides and 4 lines of symmetry, and also happens to be the only regular quadrilateral in this whole game?
quests.hint: Think of the one 4-sided shape where every side and every angle matches perfectly.
quests.explanation: A square is the only truly regular 4-sided shape here, with all equal sides and all equal angles.
quests.funFact: A rectangle and a diamond both have 4 sides, but neither has every single angle and side matching like a square.

quests.instruction: A volcano, a party hat, and a traffic cone are all real-world examples of which solid shape?
quests.hint: Think of the solid shape that is wide at the bottom and narrows smoothly to a single point.
quests.explanation: A volcano, a party hat, and a traffic cone are all shaped like a cone, wide at the base and narrowing to a point.
quests.funFact: The same basic solid shape can show up in nature, at parties, and on the road.
